details: The Federal Reserve held its federal funds rate steady at 3.50%-3.75% at its April 29 meeting, marking the third consecutive pause. Despite the official statement signaling a bias toward future rate cuts due to "modest progress" on inflation and "moderating" labor market conditions, three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) members publicly dissented. These members argued against telegraphing a cutting bias, citing core inflation remaining above 2.5% and ongoing tariff pass-through into goods prices. The latest March Core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred measure, registered 0.3% monthly, bringing the year-over-year rate to 3.2%. Headline PCE jumped 0.7% on the month and 3.5% from a year ago, the biggest annual print in nearly three years.
title: Fed Maintains Rates, Internal Dissent on Future Cuts

details: An ECB speech on May 8, 2026, highlighted the rapid growth of stablecoins, now exceeding $300 billion, and their increasing links to the traditional financial system. Europe's MiCAR brought stablecoins under regulation in 2024, aiming to mitigate risks. In the U.S., the GENIUS Act is described as a tool to ensure the continued global dominance of the U.S. dollar and cement demand for U.S. Treasuries, indicating a shift towards integrating digital assets into existing financial frameworks. The Consensus 2026 conference also emphasized crypto's movement towards traditional finance, with stablecoins emerging as practical tools for payments and liquidity management.
title: Stablecoins and Tokenization Gain Regulatory Attention and Integration

details: News of U.S. strikes in Iran on May 8, 2026, led to a brief dip in Bitcoin's price below $80,000, triggering approximately $300 million in futures liquidations and pushing oil prices above $100. While markets are currently pricing in some de-escalation, any renewed conflict could impact energy prices, inflation expectations, and risk assets, including cryptocurrencies. On-chain analytics firm CryptoQuant noted increased Bitcoin profit-taking after its recent rally, describing the price increase as a "bear market rally" and suggesting further profit realization could occur, though a significant correction might take time. Bitcoin's dominance has surpassed 60% in early May 2026.
title: Geopolitical Tensions Cause Bitcoin Dip; "Bear Market Rally" Caution Issued
